title: May a name/value Table hide its header row?
context: Table accepts headerVisible={false} and its Anatomy offers it for name/value tables. The Property table page says every name/value list has a header row. This one is still open.

current.text: Header row — the Data grid’s silver band (gray 50 to gray 200) with a gray 400 line under it, 28px tall at Compact (32 Standard, 40 Comfortable), 12px semibold titles (optional: headerVisible={false} hides it for a name/value table, whose first column names each row).

A property table is a static Table whose first column names each row (rowLabel), with the values in the columns after it: a reference of facts read across. Every name/value list of reference facts in Plenix is a Table with a header row.
headerVisible = true

current.text: The DataGrid responds to its own width: under 600px it becomes a list of its key columns, the first as the title line and the others under it, keeping the checkbox and the row actions. narrow: "table" (default inside SplitView) | "list" (default elsewhere: under narrowAt, 600px, a list of keyColumns) | "auto"
